questions.question_text: Which unit is more suitable for recording the area of a suburban park covering about $80\,000\text{ m}^{2}$?

options.why: Chose a region-sized unit that is too large for a suburban park.
Used a unit of length rather than a square unit for area.
Used a cubic unit for volume instead of a unit for land area.

questions.solution_text:
$80\,000\text{ m}^2=8\text{ ha}$.
Hectares give the more suitable-sized measure for this park.

options.why: Divided by $1\,000$ instead of by $10\,000$ square metres per hectare.
Divided by $100$ instead of by $10\,000$ square metres per hectare.
Multiplied by $10$ instead of dividing by $10\,000$ to change to a larger unit.
Multiplied by $1\,000$ instead of by $10\,000$ square metres per hectare.
Multiplied by $100$ instead of by $10\,000$ square metres per hectare.
Divided by $10\,000$ even though converting from hectares to the smaller square-metre unit requires multiplication.
Multiplied by $1\,000$ instead of by $10\,000$ square metres per hectare.
Multiplied by $100$ instead of by $10\,000$ square metres per hectare.
Divided by $10\,000$ instead of multiplying when converting hectares to square metres.

questions.question_text:
A reserve covers $857\,500\text{ m}^{2}$.
What is its area in hectares?

options.why: Divided by $1\,000$ instead of by $10\,000$ square metres per hectare.
Divided by $100\,000$ instead of by $10\,000$ square metres per hectare.
Divided by $1\,000\,000$, the square-metres-to-square-kilometres factor, instead of by $10\,000$.
